Similar to Vader, Golbez had been turned to evil by an outside influence due to traumatic experiences, primarily wore dark armor after his fall, and was a relative of the main protagonist (his brother, in this case).{{WebCite|url=http://www.1up.com/features/final-fantasy-iv-creator-conversation|text=http://www.1up.com/features/final-fantasy-iv-creator-conversation|author=Parish, Jeremy|date=2011-04-15|work=[http://www.1up.com 1up]|archivedate=20160525135954}} The incarnation of [[W:c:batman:Bane (Tom Hardy)|Bane]] in the [[Wikipedia:Batman|Batman]] film [[W:c:batman:The Dark Knight Rises|''The Dark Knight Rises'']] also takes inspiration from Vader, particularly due to his hulking size and high intellect (retained from other incarnations of the character) along with his unique mask and distinctive breathing.{{WebCite|url=http://www.accesshollywood.com/articles/the-dark-knight-rises-christopher-nolan-says-tom-hardys-bane-has-a-little-bit-of-darth-vader-120318|text=The Dark Knight Rises: Christopher Nolan Says Tom Hardy's Bane Has 'A Little Bit Of Darth Vader'|archivedate=20160410012814}} Within the rebooted ''Star Wars'' continuity, the character of [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]] is not only inspired by Vader, but aspires to be like him in-universe and has a similar appearance and personality to Anakin prior to his injuries.{{Film|VII}} Furthermore, Darth Vader's name has become a synonym for frightening evil. During the later phase of its construction, [[Wikipedia:Washington National Cathedral|Washington National Cathedral]] held a competition for children to design new [[Wikipedia:Grotesque|Grotesques]] for the west towers. One winner was [http://www.nationalcathedral.org/about/darthVader.shtml a design featuring Darth Vader]. Lucas himself once mentioned in an interview that he based Darth Vader on the android villain Hakaider from the 1972-73 live action Japanese television series ''Jinzo Ningen Kikaider'', which he watched while visiting Japan in the early 1970s. The book ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Vader]]'' explored the cultural impact of the Vader character in detail. [[File:Star_Wars_Volkswagen_Commercial.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A boy dressed as Vader in an ad for Volkswagen]] In [[2011]] and [[2012]], the luxury car company Volkswagen aired two Super Bowl commercials featuring the character of Darth Vader. The first ad was entitled "[[The Force (Volkswagen)|The Force]]" and featured a young boy wearing a costume of Darth Vader's armor. The boy attempted to use the Force to pull his parents' car to him, but ran away when the car's alarm sounded, his parents watching from the window. The 2012 commercial aired after a different ad for Volkswagen that did not feature Vader. It featured Darth Vader strangling [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Cornelius Evazan/Legends|Cornelius Evazan]] because Evazan had commented that the new commercial was more moving than the Vader one from the previous year.{{SWArchive|url=news/volkswagen_cantina_super_bowl_ad.html|text=Volkswagen Returns to the ''Star Wars'' Cantina}} ===Portrayal=== {{Quote|Finding the right voice for Darth Vader was another challenge. Lucas never intended to use the onset vocal performance of David Prowse.|Narrator Robert Clotworthy|}} Considering the drastic changes that he goes through in the ''Star Wars'' series, Anakin Skywalker has been portrayed by many actors in different media, often with numerous actors bringing the character to life within the same instalment (particularly in the [[original trilogy]]). [[File:JamesEarlJones.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The late James Earl Jones, the famous voice of Darth Vader]] Darth Vader, as he was initially established, was portrayed on-set by [[David Prowse]] in the [[original trilogy]], while [[James Earl Jones]] provided the iconic voice of the suited Vader, a role that he reprised for [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']], ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]'' and ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''.{{WebCite|url=https://www.ew.com/article/2016/06/23/darth-vader-rogue-one-star-wars|text=Darth Vader Lives!|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2016-06-23|work=Entertainment Weekly|archivedate=20180710201541}} [[Sebastian Shaw]] played the dying Anakin, his head freed from his cybernetic armor in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] featured Anakin Skywalker as a young boy of 10, a role that was landed by [[Jake Lloyd]] after thousands of auditions. [[Hayden Christensen]] played the role of Skywalker in both [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. In the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] and [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|television series]], the character of Anakin Skywalker was voiced by [[Matt Lanter]]. David Prowse was originally intended to talk in Vader's armor, although Prowse's West Country accent made Vader seem too silly, so his voice was quickly replaced. It was rumored that George Lucas considered hiring fellow filmmaker [[Wikipedia:Orson Welles|Orson Welles]] for Vader's voice, but Welles' voice was deemed too recognizable, and ultimately James Earl Jones decided to do the voice work, as the description needed for Vader to have a deep timbre and sound intimidating matched his own voice. However, Jones would not be credited until Episode V, as he felt he did not deserve the credit due to only supplying his voice for Vader. For fight scenes in V and VI, swordsman [[Bob Anderson]] wore the suit. In new footage shot for the Special Edition of the original trilogy, actor and former [[Industrial Light & Magic]] visual effects artist [[C. Andrew Nelson]] played the infamous Dark Lord. [[File:JediGhosts-ROTJ.png|thumb|left|200px|[[Hayden Christensen]] (left) as the "new" spirit of Anakin Skywalker ([[canon]]).]] [[File:Spirits_copy1.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Sebastian Shaw]] (left) as the "old" spirit of Anakin Skywalker (non-canon).]] In the original ''Return of the Jedi'', the appearance of Skywalker's redeemed Force ghost was a robust, middle-aged to elderly man with graying brown hair and a kindly face, but upon release of the Special Edition DVD version of ''Return of the Jedi'', Skywalker is in his twenties just before his fall to the dark side. George Lucas stated that redeemed Jedi would revert as a Force ghost in their pre-fall form. ''Episode I'' casting director [[Robin Gurland]] looked at three thousand different actors to play Skywalker in the film before settling on Lloyd.[[Star Wars Trivial Pursuit]] In ''Revenge of the Sith'', Hayden Christensen wore the Darth Vader suit, which was specifically designed to fit his body. His stand-in double for the UK shoot was [[Christian Simpson|Christian J Simpson]], who also played alongside the young Skywalker in Episode I as [[Bravo Six/Legends|Bravo Six]], Lt. [[Gavyn Sykes/Legends|Gavyn Sykes]]. The few lines of the suited Vader speaking are of James Earl Jones, but at one time, there was some debate over this. Some fans believed that Jones did not participate at all, since his name does not appear in the official credits of ''Revenge of the Sith'', and the voice heard in the first trailer for the movie was that of Christensen's, albeit altered digitally. The false claim was settled with the Summer 2005 issue of [[Starlog (magazine)|''Starlog'']], in which producer [[Rick McCallum]] stated they had James Earl Jones for a partial day of work on Episode III. [[File:Anakin-TCWCotF.png|thumb|right|250px|Anakin Skywalker in ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'']] In the radio drama adaptations, [[Brock Peters]] performed as Vader, with [[David Birney]] performing as Skywalker on the final episode of the [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] radio drama. Legacy audio of Peters was used for the [[canon]]ical [[2015]] release [[A New Hope Read-Along Storybook and CD|''Episode IV: A New Hope Read-Along Storybook and CD'']]. In the [[Star Wars: Clone Wars|''Clone Wars'' cartoon]], Skywalker was voiced by [[Frankie Ryan Manriquez]] as a child and [[Mat Lucas]] as an adult. In [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'' CGI series]] and its [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|feature film]] the character is voiced by [[Matt Lanter]]. For many of the ''Star Wars'' video games, including ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Force Commander]]'', and [[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']], Vader was voiced by [[Scott Lawrence]]; in more recently released titles, such as ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'', [[Matthew Sloan]], who provides the voice of Vader in the [[Wikipedia:Chad Vader: Day Shift Manager|''Chad Vader: Day Shift Manager'']] shorts, provides Vader's voice. In the Japanese localizations, [[Wikipedia:Daisuke Namikawa|Daisuke Namikawa]] acts as the voice of Anakin as an adult, while as young Anakin, [[Wikipedia:Akiko Yajima|Akiko Yajima]] provides his voice in [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|The Clone Wars]]. As Darth Vader, the voice is provided by [[Wikipedia:Tōru Ōhira|Tōru Ōhira]] in most incarnations starting with the DVD release, save for [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]] (where he is voiced by [[Wikipedia:Ryūzaburō Ōtomo|Ryūzaburō Ōtomo]]), and a number of other substitute voices in the original films. Ōhira also by proxy, reprises his role in the Japanese version of [[Soulcalibur IV|SoulCalibur IV]]. ===Non-canon content=== In the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]], an alternate ending depicts Vader successfully leaping at Kenobi during their duel on Mustafar, impaling the Jedi from behind. The Sith Lord then greets Darth Sidious upon his arrival at the mining facility and receives a new lightsaber from his master, inspecting it briefly before running Sidious through with the blade. As the Emperor falls to the floor, Vader declares the galaxy to be his, and the stormtrooper guards lower their weapons in acceptance.[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]] In the 2005 comic "[[Old Wounds]]," written and illustrated by [[Aaron McBride]], Maul survived his encounter with Kenobi on Kamino and pursued him across the galaxy. He arrived on Mustafar and encountered Skywalker still lying mortally wounded, and he initial feared it was Kenobi and that he would be unable to take his vengeance. Maul later tracked Kenobi to Polis Massa, where he learned of Luke's birth through medical records. This allowed Maul to track Luke to the Lars homestead, as he correctly anticipated that finding Anakin's son would lead Kenobi to reveal himself.{{StoryCite|book=Star Wars: Visionaries|story=Old Wounds}} In [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed|''The Force Unleashed'']], Galen Marek is presented with the choice of either confronting Palpatine or killing the injured Darth Vader. In the non-canonical option of killing Vader, Marek uses the Force to slam his former Master into various walls before using his blade and Vader's own lightsaber to impale the Sith Lord through the chest. With Vader's death, Marek replaces him as the Emperor's new apprentice and takes on the title of Lord Starkiller. Starkiller later reveals Vader's identity to Luke Skywalker during the Battle of Hoth.''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'' [[File:WhiteVader.jpg|thumb|left|100px|The redeemed Anakin Skywalker]] In ''[[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi]]'', both the Emperor and Vader sense Yoda's death on Dagobah, and Vader is dispatched to Dagobah to learn what happened. Luke surrenders himself to Palpatine's forces and is brought before Vader and the Emperor, who also captured Leia, and Vader is ordered to kill Leia by his master. When Luke defends his sister and engages the Sith Lord in a lightsaber duel, Vader refuses to accept Luke's request for peace, forcing Luke to reveal that he and Leia are Vader's children. Stunned, Vader loses an arm to Luke's blade, and Vader turns away from the dark side and begs forgiveness from his children. The Emperor disappears in the chaos that results from the Rebel Alliance's successful attack on the station, and the Skywalker children escape the station with their wounded father, who abandons his Sith title and dons an all-white version of his armor. Declaring his loyalty to his children and the Alliance, Skywalker intends to hunt down the Emperor.''[[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi]]'' In the non-canon ending to [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II|''The Force Unleashed II'']], the clone Starkiller is killed by the Dark Apprentice before he can kill Vader on Kamino, and Vader reveals that he had succeeded in perfecting the cloning process. Vader then charges the Dark Apprentice with hunting down and executing the last of the Alliance leaders. In 4 ABY of the resultant alternate timeline, Vader and the Emperor oversee the Battle of Endor from the Death Star, and he dispatches the Dark Apprentice to protect the shield-generator bunker on the forest moon, but commands him to kill everyone in his path in order to preserve the secret of his existence. However, Palpatine reveals that he is aware of the clone's existence, striking down Vader with Force lightning and forcing him to kneel as the Emperor sent his forces to destroy the clone.''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'' [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine 7|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine'' 7]] presents a Clone Wars Infinities storyline in which the Father never saved Skywalker from the dark side on Mortis, allowing the Son to kill the Father and plunge Mortis into darkness. Embracing the dark side, Skywalker defeated and abandoned Kenobi in the fiery depths of Mortis before killing Ahsoka, and he and the Son then departed Mortis in their now-repaired ship. Arriving on Coruscant, Skywalker was confronted by both Yoda and Darth Sidious, though he was able to effortlessly defeat the two unlikely allies and struck them down and became even more powerful in the process. Entering the Senate chamber, Skywalker cast down dozens of Senatorial platforms before levitating himself onto the central dais, declaring himself Emperor Skywalker of the new Galactic Empire.[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine 7|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine'' 7]] [[File:Damaged_Darth_Vader.jpg|thumb|left|Darth Vader, damaged by a [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raider]], holds [[Tao (Sith Apprentice)|Tao's]] dead body.]] Ultimately giving up on recreating Starkiller, but still determined to gain an apprentice so he could overthrow Sidious, Vader eventually traveled to the planet of [[Shumari]], already being subjugated by the Imperials, under the pretense of completing the destruction of the planet's Jedi fugitives. The Sith Lord then engaged several Jedi and took them down effortlessly, eventually saving [[Unidentified bearded Human Jedi|their leader]] for last. Although ultimately successful in defeating the Jedi, a surviving Jedi youngling named [[Tao (Sith Apprentice)|Tao]], enraged at the death of the Jedi leader, sees Vader and stares him down in rage. Vader ultimately saw use in the boy, and made him his second secret apprentice. He trained the boy in the ways of the dark side, and like Marek before him, he also dropped him on Honoghr to survive and fight a Noghri Death Commando party unarmed. Despite his potential, however, Vader was not able to get the boy to become fully immersed in the dark side. Upon discovering this information, Vader let his apprentice, Tao, go free. Tao had been unable to display the anger and hatred necessary to embrace the dark side anyway, and Vader planned to train his newly found son in his place. It was only then that Tao displayed his anger toward Vader but, upon leaving, was captured by the Emperor himself. While Palpatine officially conferred upon Vader the newly christened ''Executor'', he also brought Tao before Vader and ordered him to strike Tao down to prove his loyalty. Though he did not want to, Vader was unable to control his body and soon slashed his lightsaber through Tao's torso. Vader, distraught at what he had been forced to do, took the near-dead Tao to his home planet of Shumari to die where he had been born. While there, Vader was attacked by [[KkH'Oar'Rrhr]], who had been tracking him ever since Vader had destroyed his village and killed his family. Hoar quickly gained an advantage over Vader, damaging his armor and revealing the lightsabers which he had built into his gaderfii. Just as the Tusken was about to strike Vader down, Tao rose from the brink of death and struck it down, saving Vader's life. Just before he died, Tao pleaded with Vader to let go of his hatred and not let the Emperor control him; Tao still sensed some good within his master. After carving a small monument to Tao, Vader returned to his former home on Tatooine briefly to contemplate the fact that he now had a son. ===Dark Lord of the Brick=== ====An unscripted appearance==== {{Quote|So, Master Yoda, we meet again! [Making lightsaber noises]''"
"''Darth! Darth. Darth, would you come here for a second? Hi. You're not in this scene either.''"
"''But imagine the audience's surprise as my lightsaber comes right off the screen—''"

"''—and into their faces.''"

"''Sorry, George.|Darth Vader and George Lucas|''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace]]''}} Airing in 2011, the non-canon TV special ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace]]'', set sometime during the Clone Wars, included appearances from Skywalker and Darth Vader. As Darth Sidious and Asajj Ventress cackled about their theft of the Republic's secret battle plans, Vader appeared, interrupting the moment by joining in their manical laughter. Filming of the scene was cut, and Vader was taken aside by George Lucas, who showed the Sith Lord that he was not in the script. Leading him away, Lucas then offered Vader a donut. Anakin Skywalker appeared dueling Grievous aboard the ''Invisible Hand'', pausing for a photograph by Bobby, a Jedi initiate on a school bus full of younglings. Later, Vader returned on the Hoth, where Yoda and the orphan "Ian" had crash-landed, swinging his lightsaber at the Jedi Master. Lucas reappeared and again told Vader that he was not a part of the scene. As Vader began to explain how his saber would explode off the screen to the surprise of the audience, Lucas kicked him off of the set. Vader obliged, apologizing to Lucas. ====Striking out==== =====The phantom apprentice===== {{Quote|[To Palpatine] Exellency, our probes have spotted the ''Millenium Falcon''. It's on its way to Naboo to meet Luke Skywalker.''"
"''I will go and personally crush him. Then you'll see who's the most fearsome Sith Lord in the galaxy.''"
[Vader leaves; beat; re-enters]
"''That was a closet.|Piett and Vader|''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Out]]''}} A year later, Vader appeared in the 2012 special ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Out]]''. Aboard the ''Executor''{{'s}} bridge, Vader's arrival was heralded by a frightened officer who fell into one of the crew pits. Entering belatedly at the urging of the director, Vader instructed Admiral Ozzel to find the rebels responsible for destroying the Death Star. Ozzel informed Vader of his galaxy-wide dispersal of Imperial probe droids, dispatched to hunt down Skywalker. Several probes hovered around Vader, having located the wrong Skywalker, causing Ozzel to shoo them away. Vader told Ozzel that though he had failed him for the last time, he would be allowed to live, causing Captain Piett to interject that by doing so, Ozzel could fail Vader again. A squabble broke out between Ozzel, Piett, and General Veers, causing Vader to strangle them with the Force, force them to punch one another, and knock them out, disparaging the trio as "mutton-heads." Later, Emperor Palpatine consulted with Vader about a brilliant plan to punish the rebels for destroying the Death Star: to build another Death Star. Beginning to say that another Death Star would be stupid, Vader quickly changed his tune. Summoning a box of parts, Palpatine stated his desire to build the superweapon together with his "boys," causing Vader to do a double-take. Emerging on to the bridge, Palpatine's other apprentice, Darth Maul, put on a performance that displayed his octo-bladed lightsaber. Maul landed in front of Vader, who considered the Zabrak to be a show-off. Maul and Vader dueled, trading insults. Vader used the Force to choke Maul; Maul turned the choke back towards Vader, and Vader resorted to choking the Sith with his other hand. Plaptine blasted the duo with Force lightning, instructing them to play nice as Piett reported that probe droids had discovered the ''Millenium Falcon'' en route to Naboo. Vader declared his intent to go there and crush them to Maul before mistakenly entering a closet, then leaving. In his TIE Advanced X1, Vader encountered Skywalker, who had disguised himself as Vader to escape a mob of fangirls, flying his X-wing in space. Colliding into one another, the two rebuilt their starfighters, remarking on the oddity of the situatuon. Crash-landing on Tatooine, Vader cried out as his helmet had become infested with sand. Immediately, the Sith Lord was ambushed by Jawas. The scavengers disabled his armor with an ion blaster, causing Vader to collapse. =====Sons and masters===== {{Quote|Vader.''"
"''Uh-oh.''"
"''Because of you, both my new Death Star and Darth Maul are no more. That's my boy! [chuckles]''"
"''Hugs mean love.|Emperor Palpatine and Vader|}} Adorned with junk and hanging from a sandcrawler, Vader was sprayed in the helmet by a Jawa. The Sith Lord appealed to the Jawa's customer: Watto, his old master, but the Toydarian dismissed Vader as a "crazy droid." Angered, Vader burst free and rearranged the sandcrawler into a playground before escaping in Anakin Skywalker's podracer. The Sith Lord then reported in to his master, relaying that he had found the rebels. Palpatine questioned his appearance, causing Maul to chuckle as Vader offered no explanation. Vader arrived on Naboo and exposed Skywalker, who was impersonating the Sith, to Veers. Drawing his lightsaber, Vader cited pleasure at finally encountering the boy, who retorted that Vader had killed his father. As Vader prepared to reveal his identity, Skywalker was mobbed by his fangirls, irritating Vader at the interruption of his devastating revelation. Vader began to reiterate himself, but was interrupted by Luke's droids, C-3PO and R2-D2, who produced a dreamy picture of Anakin Skywalker, causing the fangirls to mob Vader instead. Vader pursued Skywalker in their respective starfighters. His son in his crosshairs, the Sith Lord was knocked off course by the fangirls. Asking if their parents knew where they were, Vader jumped to hyperspace, the girls hot on his trail. Emerging from lightspeed, Vader crashed into the newly-finished Darth Star, a Death Star built by Maul in his own image. Returning to the ''Executor'', Vader was confronted by Palpatine for destroying the Darth Star and ejecting Maul into space. Surprisingly, Palpatine praised Vader, hugging his apprentice, a gesture Vader took as an act of love. Later, Vader attended a ceremony. Palpatine awarded him a medal as a bisected Maul looked on in disdain. The Sith was mobbed by his fangirls, one of whom requested to see his face. Vader removed his helmet, frightening the girls, who then turned their attention toward chasing Vader's rival instead. Laughing, Vader clapped one of the attending stormtroopers on the back, causing the rest to fall like dominoes and earning a reprimand from his master. ====The Sith clone menace==== =====Adventures in babysitting===== {{Quote|You're not gonna freeze, I'll show you. See, I'm out here and I'm okay.''"
[Skywalker is trampled by a tauntaun]
"''That was a one of a kind, freak—''"
[Skywalker is trampled by a wampa and a rancor]
"''Meanwhile, Obi-Wan gets to have all the fun.|Anakin Skywalker|{{YodaChronicles|Menace of the Sith}}}} In 2013, ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Yoda Chronicles]]'' premiered. Yoda's Padawans, Rako, Bene, Vaash Ti, and Bobby observed a recording of Skywalker stored in a holocron. Skywalker, his AT-RT blown up by droidekas, demolished the destroyer droids with his lightsaber to the applause of the young Jedi. Suddenly, Yoda felt a disturbance in the Force, causing him to drop the holocron, ending the display. Skywalker was later present at a ceremony honoring the Padawans for stopping the threat sensed by Yoda, the Sith clone Jek-14, though Jek had escaped into the galaxy.{{YodaChronicles|The Phantom Clone}} As Yoda investigated Jek, Skywalker was assigned as a substitute teacher to chaperone the Padawans on a field trip. As Skywalker complained about the assignment, R2-D2 played a recording of Obi-Wan Kenobi telling him to learn his place, which Skywalker claimed was taken out of context. At the inquiry of Bobby, Skywalker produced a book, reading aloud that their destination was one with an important history to the Jedi, leading Rako to dejectedly guess Hoth. Skywalker tried to encourage the Padawans, but Vaash Ti kindly let the Jedi down that he wasn't a very good actor. Landing the Jedi temple school bus, Skywalker ushered the younglings to a nearby cave. Walking outside, Skywalker claimed he was not cold, only to be run over by a tauntaun. Putting the occurrence down as a freak accident, Skywalker was quickly trampled by a wampa and a rancor. As the Padawans laughed at his misfortune, Skywalker remarked that Kenobi got to have all the fun. Later, the Padawans played with Skywalker's cybernetic arm, attaching it to a snowman as the Jedi consulted with C-3PO. Skywalker told 3PO he appreciated his assistance as Rako suggested that it would be cool if Skywalker's entire body was robotic. C-3PO informed Skywalker that all the Jedi were on the hunt for Jek-14, frustrating him that he was stuck on the ice planet. The Padawans used the cybernetic arm to pelt Skywalker with a snowball, earning his ire, and 3PO apologized as he had to cut the conversation short. =====Attack of the Skywalker===== {{Quote|That's him! Wait 'til the Council hears about this. Not ready. Ha!''"
[Skywalker produces a comlink]
"''Master Yoda, I've found the Sith clone. I've got him here.''"
[Skywalker charges]
"''Surrender, Sith clone!|Anakin Skywalker|}} As Skywalker again expressed his exasperation at supervising the Padawans, Rako suggested that the Jedi Council had a reason for assigning him the task. Believing that the Council wanted him to clear his mind of distractions, Skywalker countered that he did not have distractions, believing that he was "ready" and, as the Chosen One, would bring balance to the Force and was capable of anything. Skywalker then noticed that the Padawans had disappeared. Skywalker located the Padawans, who had found none other than Jek. Comm-ing in his findings to Yoda, Skywalker drew his weapon and charged the clone, only to bounce off of a large Force shield. The noise attracted the attention of Separatist probe droids, also in search of Jek, who blew his starship out of the sky, allowing him to be retrieved by General Grievous aboard the ''Soulless One''. R2-D2 tended to Skywalker, who reflected that he may be overly impulsive. The astromech droid in turn called him "Einstein," of whom Skywalker was not aware. Skywalker reported the incident to the Council, who suspected that Count Dooku would use an army of Jek clones to attack Coruscant. Kenobi chided Skywalker for his behavior, instructing him not to return to join the upcoming conflict as redemption for his earlier mistake. As the Separatist flagship ''Malevolence'' emerged above Coruscant—and the Jedi school bus—Skywalker admitted that Kenobi's request was no longer a possibility. Bringing the bus around, Skywalker opened fire on the Separatist vulture droids, destroying one. Below, Yoda blamed Kenobi for ignoring his earlier warnings not to train Skywalker. Kenobi pointed out that he did so to fulfill Qui-Gon Jinn's dying wish, but Jinn appeared as a Force ghost and placed the fault on Kenobi for Skywalker's training. =====A different battle of Coruscant===== {{Quote|Padawans, we're not done yet. Remember Jek and create.''"
"''Great idea, Anakin.''"
"''Anakin, I never thought I'd say this, but you actually taught me something.''"
"''That's nothing. Watch this.''"
[Skywalker makes an attack run on the ''Malevolence'']
"''I can't believe this ship didn't have a tiny vulnerable spot that if you shoot it, it'll make the whole thing blow up.|Anakin Skywalker, Vaash Ti, and Rako|}} The Jedi school bus was destroyed by a vulture droid, leaving Skywalker and the Padawans floating in space. In the spirit of Jek, Skywalker led the Padawans to rebuild the remains of the bus into personal starfighters, garnering praise from Vaash Ti and Rako. Skywalker then made an attack run against the ''Malevolence'', though it was unsuccessful, causing him to lament the lack of a critical weakness in the ship's design. Asajj Ventress destroyed Skywalker's fighter, sending him flying into the Malevolence{{'s}} hull. The Jedi then noticed precisely the vulnerability he was looking for. Inserting his lightsaber into the port, Skywalker's actions flushed a group of B1 battle droids into space and resulted in the destruction of the warship. Skywalker and the Padawans regrouped, and Skywalker informed Yoda of their victory and that they were headed his way. Chancellor Palpatine, secretly Darth Sidious, prevented Dooku and Grievous from crash-landing, and the Separatist leaders deployed their army of Jek clones. The original Jek-14 sided with the Jedi, dispelling his clones' attacks and sending the Separatists running. However, Jek desired to remain independent; Skywalker and the other Jedi waved to the Sith clone as he departed in a Z-95 Headhunter. When Yoda recorded the Padawans' achievements in a Jedi holocron, Bene attributed Skywalker as crucial to their heroics. Yoda noted Skywalker's valor and, recognizing the need for his return to the front lines of the war, indicated that C-3PO would return as the Padawans' teacher. Qui-Gon Jinn appeared to take to credit for Skywalker's accomplishments, but Kenobi, cross with Jinn's apparent double standard, chased him around the room. =====Nearing war's end===== {{Quote|Yeah? Well, good luck putting a dozen ships back together, genius.''"
"''Who said a dozen?''"
[Jek-14 rebuilds the Republic fleet into one large cruiser]
"''I don't believe it.''"
"''That… is why you fail.|Anakin Skywalker and Jek-14|{{YodaChronicles|Attack of the Jedi}}}} After a Republic victory on Geonosis, Skywalker steadied a disoriented Yoda, asking the Jedi Master if he knew what it meant. Yoda concurred that a medal ceremony was in order, to Skywalker, Kenobi, and the Padawans' delight. Chancellor Palpatine reported the outcome to the Senate, and Bail Organa proposed that the most pressing issue was funding for a post-war victory celebration. Palpatine attempted to temper expectations, claiming the war was far from over, but Kenobi, informed by Commander Cody, indicated that the Sith were all in one place—on Mustafar. Yoda suggested a strike to wipe them all out, eliciting a smirk from Skywalker, and Palpatine approved, causing the Senate to party. Palpatine attempted to sneak off to Mustafar to join the Sith as Darth Sidious, but caught by Yoda, Kenobi, and Skywalker, claimed he wanted to come along and witness the Republic's success. Aware of his value, Kenobi and Skywalker accompanied the Chancellor as bodyguards, and C-3PO joined the trio in his capacity as a protocol droid. Skywalker indicated that the Chancellor must be excited for the defeat of the Sith, which Palpatine reluctantly agreed to, though hedged that "evil was everywhere" and that there were "heroes on both sides." Kenobi shot down the idea, and Skywalker gestured that the Chancellor was crazy. Grievous attempted to contact Palpatine, who shut down the call, then tried to retrieve him in person in the ''Soulless One''. As Palpatine disavowed any association, Skywalker took the controls, pursuing the Separatist cyborg and opening fire. Grievous disappeared into an asteroid field, but was quickly surrounded by the Republic fleet. As Grievous escaped into hyperspace, Yoda ordered Republic forces to follow, but with all of the starships on the same trajectory, the fleet collided and was destroyed. Skywalker and Kenobi debated how to put the ships back together, with Skywalker jamming a part where it did not belong. Yoda called out the Jedi and their arguing as unhelpful. Bene suggested an ally nearby who could reconstruct the fleet. Skywalker objected, as all of the Jedi were present, but Bene admitted that who she had in mind was not a Jedi. Traveling to Endor in the Jedi school bus, Yoda and the Padawans brought Jek-14 to help. Jek took note of the disastrous state of the fleet, causing Skywalker to dismiss his help, though Jek remarked that they were "doing great so far" without him. Skywalker sarcastically wished Jek luck, as rebuilding the fleet was a nearly impossible task. Jek instead combined the destroyed ships into one massive cruiser, to Skywalker's disbelief. =====Mustafar and boogie time===== {{Quote|Something wrong, Anakin?''"

"''Indeed. Well, I think you're a great Jedi.''"

"''And you're an excellent judge of character.|Chancellor Palpatine and Anakin Skywalker|}} Arriving at Mustafar, Yoda, Kenobi, and Skywalker descended to confront the Sith with an acrobatic flip. Skywalker engaged in a duel with Ventress, which was shortly interrupted by supporting fire from the Republic cruiser, causing the dark acolyte to retreat. Chancellor Palpatine, who had arrived on Mustafar by his own means, coordinated an ambush, leading the Jedi's clone troopers to be killed by the Sith and the Republic cruiser to be destroyed by a thermal detonator. With a newfound advantage, the Sith redoubled their attack. Forced back on to rocks amongst the lava, the Jedi were saved by the arrival of Jek, who destroyed the Klegger Corp Mining Facility and repaired the Republic cruiser, offering the Jedi a ride home. Later, at a victory celebration, Skywalker sat alone, frustrated by all of the focus and attention on Jek, as he was the Chosen One. Perceiving an opportunity, Palpatine complimented Skywalker as a great Jedi, who in turn told the Chancellor he was a good man. Palpatine replied that he thought Skywalker was an excellent judge of character. ===Translations=== *In the Italian original and prequel trilogies, he's know as '''Lord Dart Fener'''.
